articles.title: Jane Fonda’s former 1924 Hollywood Hills home is back on the market for $1.99 million; she lived there during two marriages, while the CIA illegally surveilled her and intercepted her mail
articles.summary: Jane Fonda’s former home in the Hollywood Hills is now on the market, asking $1.99 million, according to a report by the New York Post.
articles.body: Jane Fonda’s former home in the Hollywood Hills is now on the market, asking $1.99 million, according to a report by the New York Post. The Mediterranean Revival villa, built in 1932, sits at the end of a tranquil cul-de-sac in Whitley Heights, Hollywood’s first National Register historic district. The idyllic mansion at 2001 Holly Hill Terrace is one of only two homes in the neighbourhood protected by a Los Angeles Conservancy façade easement, according to the listing.The home’s past goes well beyond its stucco walls. Jane Fonda lived there for a time while she was married to French film director Roger Vadim. They wed in 1965 and divorced in 1973. Later, she lived in the same house with her second husband, the political activist Tom Hayden, according to LA city planning records. Fonda never owned the house; she rented it.Fonda was once surveilled by the CIA while living hereThis Hollywood Hills mansion has seen many phases of Fonda’s life. She had become one of the most visible critics of the Vietnam War, and the government took notice. While living in the house, she came under surveillance by the CIA. The agency famously intercepted and opened her mail. A document declassified in 2018 shows Fonda’s name and the Holly Hill Terrace address on a list of 50 people the agency tracked in 1971. Records from the period also show that the CIA acquired four letters sent to her from the Soviet Union. The agency opened them in secret, according to National Security Archive documents. “That is illegal, and we stopped it in 1973,” then CIA Director William Colby reportedly told President Gerald Ford in 1975.Inside the Mediterranean Revival villaWhitley Heights has seen plenty of change in a century, but nothing like this. According to the listing, this is “one of the houses that has defined Whitley Heights for a century”. Developer H.J. Whitley built the home as his last project in Whitley Heights. He designed the neighbourhood to look like an Italian hillside village, and it became home to Old Hollywood names. Rudolph Valentino, Bette Davis and Jean Harlow all lived nearby at one point.The house has a two-storey veranda, added in 1941, and two entrances. It has five bedrooms and five bathrooms. From Holly Hill Terrace, a grand staircase climbs to the front door. From Grace Avenue, a driver can pull into a two-car garage that opens straight into the house. The steps from there lead to the pool and a garden full of fruit trees.The main floor has a living room, a home office and a library. Both the office and the library open onto a patio with canyon views. There is also a formal dining room on this floor, along with a large kitchen with a breakfast nook. This floor also has a bedroom with a small bathroom. Another compact bathroom opens onto the pool deck.Upstairs, the primary suite includes a sitting area, its own patio with canyon and treetop views, and a bathroom with a soaking tub, a separate shower and a large wardrobe. Two more bedrooms share a full bathroom. Access is another highlight. The studios, the Hollywood Bowl and Franklin Village are a short drive away, and the freeways to downtown and the Valley are close by.The seller is Kathleen Whyte, the daughter of character actors Bryan Clark and Jo Deodato Clark. The couple bought the home in 1985 for $234,180 and lived there for 41 years. The house first hit the market in 2024 at $2.79 million. It is now listed at $1.99 million, about $800,000 less.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: 'Time for Ukraine to get new president,' says Trump after Zelensky condemns diesel deal
articles.summary: Ukraine's leader had said the deal with Russia to release diesel into the US would help Moscow fund the war.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has said he thinks "it's time for Ukraine to get a new president" as he responded to Volodymyr Zelensky's criticism of the US diesel deal with Russia.

The Ukrainian president warned a new deal to release millions of tonnes of Russian diesel into the US would provide Moscow with money to continue its war against his nation, calling it a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump told reporters outside the White House on Saturday that Zelensky "wants to make problems for the world" by continuing to authorise attacks on Russian refineries.

"He'd better damn well stop," Trump said, before suggesting Ukraine should "get a new leader who can make a deal".

Russia and Ukraine have recently intensified their strikes, targeting energy-generating and transport facilities, as well as major logistics hubs.

"We said, 'you can do whatever you want to Russia, don't hit the refineries', because that's a world problem that's caused," he said.

"He could have made many deals and for some reason, he never does."

Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev described Trump's intervention as "iconic and historic", saying that Ukraine "needs leadership actually focused on peace".

The US president confirmed on Friday that an agreement had been reached with Moscow to suspend sanctions on Russian diesel exports until 7 April.

Zelensky reacted by saying it would allow Moscow to raise new funds to source new military equipment to continue the war.

He also accused Moscow of taking the deal "to mean they can keep fighting, to mean they keep dropping bombs on cities" following deadly new strikes on Zaporizhzhia.

Analysis: Trump's shock Russia deal highlights mounting pressure to curb fuel prices

The Ukrainian president spoke to several allies on Saturday to discuss the latest developments, calling for "real decisions to protect lives in Ukraine" and to protect European security.

A Downing Street spokesperson said UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham had spoken to Zelensky and that the pair had agreed Russia should acquiesce to "an immediate energy ceasefire" and end its attacks on shipping in the Black Sea.

"This would immediately release more energy and food supplies into the global market," the spokesperson added.

News of the US-Russia diesel deal was also met with criticism by EU's foreign affairs chief Kaja Kallas, who echoed Zelensky in saying that suspending sanctions "provides Moscow with more revenues to wage war", adding: "This is not the time to ease pressure on Russia, and Europe won't."

She said European foreign ministers intended to approve the biggest set of sanctions on Russia since the start of its full-scale invasion on Monday.

The deal with Russia is the latest effort from Trump to lower fuel prices in the US ahead of the midterm elections, after months spent grappling with the political consequences of the Iran war.

That conflict, which began in February, has sent the cost of petrol and in particular diesel skyrocketing, which has soured his standing with the American public who have been stung by the higher pump prices and knock-on effects that led to across-the-board inflation.

The average price of diesel is currently $6.28 (£4.74) a gallon, according to the AAA – up from last month's $5.94 average, and $3.68 last year.

Under the deal, Russia would release an initial 300,000 tonnes of diesel "to the American and global marketplace" followed by an additional 500,000 tonnes in November.

A further million would follow, Trump wrote on Truth Social, and then another 3m tonnes "within a short period of time" – but he noted that this delivery will be "based on the condition of their diesel refineries".

In the past 10 months, Russia experienced two waves of severe fuel shortages across the country due to Ukrainian drones strikes on its oil refineries.

Diesel production in Russia dropped by an estimated 30%, according to the International Energy Agency.

Trump had already called for new elections in Ukraine last December , saying Ukrainian voters should have the choice to replace Zelensky.

Since the war broke out in 2022 Ukraine has been under martial law, meaning elections are suspended.

articles.title: In Brazil, a 69-year-old farmer spent 20 years building his own Italian-style stone house, one rock at a time, finally completing the project he began mostly alone
articles.summary: Discover the inspiring journey of Dionísio Bertoldi, a Brazilian farmer who spent two decades constructing his own Italian-style stone house, learning masonry skills along the way and honoring his family's heritage.
articles.body: A farmer in Brazil, 69, spent two decades turning about 2,000 stones into a house with inspiration drawn from the stone homes of Italy. Dionísio Bertoldi started the project in 1995 after his first marriage and completed it in 2015, building almost the entire residence by himself.As reported by NSC Total, Bertoldi, hailing from the Ipiranga community in Rodeio, Santa Catarina, was not a mason by profession when he began building, and as the project progressed he learned how to work with the material. He estimated that if he knew how to cut and shape the stone, the house would have taken two to three years rather than twenty to finish. The long construction was hindered by personal events. After the death of his first child during childbirth and other deaths in the family, Bertoldi lost the motivation to continue and moved to a neighbouring area. The construction was halted for almost a decade until he resumed and completed it in 2015.Building with thousands of stones By his own account, Bertoldi sourced some of the raw materials from his property and others were bought locally. He learned the best techniques and tools, and spent the rest of his available time on construction while working as a farmer. Rather than relying on the expertise of a masonry crew, the process required him to select, break and position the stones, some weighing up to two tonnes by his estimate. He recalled repeatedly striking his hands with a sledgehammer and being attacked by bees while collecting stone in wooded areas.The only outside support he received came during the second part of the slab work, when a friend and two bricklayers helped out for half a day, after which Bertoldi continued on his own. The end product of his labour was a finished house containing 10 rooms, neither plastered nor painted in order to preserve the exposed stone and its rustic appearance. The walls measured about 25 centimetres in thickness, the doors were made by Bertoldi himself, and the windows carried several Italian flags, reinforcing the visual connection to the inspiration behind the project.A house built around family heritageThe Italian connection is personal for Bertoldi, who told ND Mais his grandparents came from Italy and worked as architects building churches in the region. He’s also descended from the Bertoldi, Feltrin, and Fiamoncini families, weaving the house into a history of Italian immigration. This was the reason for choosing the stones, which carried more than a construction decision, because he wanted a home that embodied his family’s country of origin while preserving a cultural connection that had been carried into Brazil. That connection extends beyond the house itself, as Bertoldi also makes wine and sings in Italian.The completed house has garnered attention beyond the local community as the story spread on social media, which led to his being recognised in Italy during a visit. Bertoldi has highlighted the practical characteristics of the house, stating that during the summers it stays cool, and in winters it retains warmth and does not accumulate moisture.The thermal characteristics of traditional Italian buildings built from stone have also been examined through the lens of academic research and help provide context for Bertoldi's own observation. A 2013 study in Building and Environment investigated the Sassi of Matera and the Trulli of Alberobello and found that these structures helped maintain relatively stable indoor temperatures through different seasons and limited the effect of outdoor temperature fluctuations. However, those were traditional buildings in Italy and not Bertoldi's residence, so the study can only provide architectural context rather than independent evidence of the thermal performance of his house.You use AI every day. articles.title: Protest with no one address: How CJP’s 'Jantar Mantar 2.0' call outgrew its venue, spread across cities
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: By the time Saturday drew to a close, the protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had stretched far beyond its planned venue
articles.body: NEW DELHI: By the time Saturday drew to a close, the protest against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had stretched far beyond its planned venue at Jantar Mantar.In Delhi, thousands were detained before the Cockroach Janta Party’s (CJP) demonstration could take shape.In Mumbai and Bengaluru, solidarity protests ran into police barricades and detentions, while Ahmedabad saw activists and students detained during a separate gathering.The CJP had called for ‘Jantar Mantar 2.0’ to demand Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Its founder Abhijeet Dipke and other senior leaders were detained after arriving in Delhi from Mumbai. By the end of the day, police had detained more than 7,000 people in the capital, while hundreds more were held during demonstrations elsewhere.All the detainees were released by Delhi Police later in evening, except the 3 party leaders where due legal process will be followed, police sources quoted by news agency ANI quoted.Delhi: A protest stopped before it could gather paceDelhi Police detained more than 7,000 people attempting to reach Jantar Mantar, among them Dipke, co-convenor Saurav Das, leader Ashutosh Ranka, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee and several Left leaders and activists.Former Kerala chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan was also detained along with other CPI(M) leaders.Police had denied permission for the CJP demonstration, citing public safety, traffic management and law-and-order concerns.Barricades went up along routes leading to Jantar Mantar, personnel were deployed at key locations and drones were used to monitor movement. Detentions were reported near Regal Cinema, Minto Bridge and Akashwani Bhawan.Stone pelting was reported near Akashwani Bhawan which left two police personnel injured.The day also saw a political face-off over the crackdown. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and Kejriwal of trying to turn the capital into a “battleground” with the CJP, which she called their “B-Team”.Delhi BJP president and Union minister Harsh Malhotra described the planned demonstration as a “complete flop”.For those detained, however, the day did not end with their arrest. Vijayan, 82, said police made him, Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas and Kerala MLA KN Balagopal travel around Delhi in a vehicle for nearly three-and-a-half hours before taking them to Mandir Marg police station.Brittas alleged that police had not taken Vijayan’s age and health into account or ensured he received his medicines on time. The leaders were released by evening.Mumbai: Tushar Gandhi, Imran Khan among 600 detainedIn Mumbai, the call for solidarity brought protesters to August Kranti Maidan, Hutatma Chowk and other locations.Around 600 people were detained across the city, including activist Tushar Gandhi, great-grandson of Mahatma Gandhi, actor Imran Khan and CPI(M) workers.Around 200 people were detained at August Kranti Maidan, where members of Gandhi’s organisation, ‘Hum Bharat Ke Log’, and CPI(M) activists had gathered. Workers of the Vanchit Bahujan Aghadi also protested at Hutatma Chowk.DCP Ragasudha R said the detained protesters had been released, while further legal proceedings were underway.She said around 400 people were detained at Nana Chowk near August Kranti Maidan, where around 500 police personnel had been deployed. Registration of FIRs was in progress.Khan offered a wry account of his detention from inside a police van: “Apparently, I am going for a drive.” In a video that surfaced later, he questioned why he was being manhandled and said he was not part of any organisation.Tushar Gandhi, who was picked up from Bandra and taken to DN Nagar police station, was released around nine hours later.Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aditya Thackeray visited the police station seeking his release. Some protesters alleged that police had manhandled them during the detentions.Police said preventive action was taken because August Kranti Maidan is not a designated protest site under a Bombay high court order.Bengaluru: Students stopped short of EC officeIn Bengaluru, the protest took the form of a march that never reached its destination.Student organisations, including AISA, SFI, AIDSO and AISF, gathered at Freedom Park and attempted to march towards the Election Commission office, demanding the scrapping of the SIR process and Kumar’s resignation.Heavy police deployment and barricades blocked their way, according to AISA Karnataka.The organisation alleged that protesters were detained when they tried to bypass the barricades and condemned the action as suppression of the right to protest.It demanded the release of those detained, removal of the barricades and permission for the demonstration to proceed peacefully.The EC office was only a few hundred metres from Freedom Park, the organisation said.Ahmedabad: Detentions on the streets, allegations of house arrestIn Ahmedabad, several political activists and members of Gen-Z were detained as they gathered near Ellisbridge in the evening. They raised slogans including “vote thief, step down”, “remove Gyanesh Kumar” and “save democracy”.NSUI leader Shubham Thakar, who had earlier waved black flags at Kumar’s convoy during the CEC’s visit to Ahmedabad, was among those detained. Activist Subodh Parmar said organisers had sought permission for a gathering near MJ Library but were denied it.The street protests followed allegations by activists that police had visited their homes or kept them under house arrest ahead of the Delhi demonstration.Activist Dev Desai claimed police were stationed outside his home from Friday morning until Saturday morning. Theatre director Savan Zalariya said police visited his home and questioned him about plans to travel to Delhi or organise a local demonstration.Ahmedabad police commissioner Anupam Singh Gehlot said action had been taken as required and that nobody was under detention at the time of his statement.The preparations for the Delhi protest had also had a knock-on effect on rail travel. articles.title: US death row inmate Christa Pike returns to prison from hospital after surviving lethal injection execution
articles.summary: Christa Pike, the Tennessee death row inmate who survived an attempt to execute her by lethal injection, has returned to prison after spending more than a
articles.body: Christa Pike, the Tennessee death row inmate who survived an attempt to execute her by lethal injection, has returned to prison after spending more than a week in hospital. Her lawyers said Saturday that the 50-year-old had been discharged and was continuing to receive medical care.Pike was transferred to the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center in Nashville, the women's prison where she had been held for three decades. Her return comes amid mounting questions over how Tennessee's execution procedure failed despite the administration of two doses of a lethal drug.“She is grateful to the first responders and her medical team for their care in these extraordinary circumstances,” her attorneys said in a statement, as quoted by the Associated Press. “She is continuing to receive medical care at the prison, and we will continue to track her recovery.”The September 30 incident has drawn national attention because Pike is believed to be the first person known to have survived after receiving lethal injection drugs during an execution.What happened?Pike was taken to hospital after the state failed to carry out her execution using pentobarbital, the drug in Tennessee's lethal injection protocol. She remained unconscious and was placed on a ventilator as doctors treated her. Her attorneys initially feared she would not survive.The execution had begun with Pike telling witnesses she was at peace. About five minutes later, she raised her head and complained that her arm hurt. She subsequently appeared to lose consciousness, but witnesses reported that she continued breathing heavily. An ambulance eventually took her to hospital.The precise cause of the failure remains unclear. Tennessee officials have not publicly explained what went wrong, while medical and lethal-injection experts have raised concerns about the placement of the intravenous lines. One possibility is that the drug entered surrounding tissue instead of reaching her bloodstream.Pike's lawyers alleged in a court filing that “apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realize that the IV lines were not correctly placed.”A judge has since ordered state officials to preserve evidence related to the failed execution, as Pike's legal team seeks answers about the procedure and its consequences.Governor orders review, prison chief resignsThe incident has prompted a wider review of Tennessee's execution practices. Governor Bill Lee suspended all remaining scheduled executions for 2026 and ordered an independent, third-party investigation to establish what happened.Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada also announced his resignation following the failed execution. The developments have intensified scrutiny of the state's lethal injection procedures, particularly because this was its second failed execution attempt in 2026.Pike was sentenced to death for the 1995 beating and stabbing murder of her classmate, Colleen Slemmer, who was 19 at the time. Pike was 18 when she committed the crime.Her return to prison marks a new stage in the aftermath of the failed execution, but major questions remain over the medical complications she suffered and the circumstances that prevented the state from carrying out the sentence. The independent review is expected to examine the procedure, while her lawyers continue to challenge the state's handling of the execution.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Florida cybersecurity owner accused of misleading ransomware victims; prosecutors allege his firm charged them over $19 million while secretly paying hackers more than $8 million
articles.summary: A Florida cybersecurity company owner who allegedly told ransomware victims that his firm could recover encrypted data without paying hackers is now
articles.body: A Florida cybersecurity company owner who allegedly told ransomware victims that his firm could recover encrypted data without paying hackers is now facing federal wire fraud charges. According to the US Department of Justice (DOJ), Zohar Pinhasi, 50, owner of ransomware remediation company MonsterCloud, claimed to have proprietary tools and advanced techniques for decrypting files. Prosecutors allege that his company instead paid the cybercriminals behind the attacks and charged clients substantially more for the recovery. The DOJ said Pinhasi allegedly collected more than $19 million from clients while secretly paying over $8 million in ransom.What prosecutors allegePinhasi, who is also known as “Zack Silver” and “Zack Green,” was arraigned in federal court in Brooklyn on October 7 after being indicted by a grand jury in the Eastern District of New York on September 23. He is accused of defrauding clients who turned to MonsterCloud after their businesses were hit by ransomware. Ransomware attacks typically lock or encrypt a victim's computer files and demand payment in exchange for restoring access. According to the indictment described by the DOJ, Pinhasi presented MonsterCloud as an alternative to paying those demands. The company's website reportedly advised businesses not to pay ransomware attackers and said its team could recover data without giving in to ransom demands.Pinhasi allegedly told prospective clients that MonsterCloud used “proprietary tools” and “advanced decryption techniques” to recover encrypted information. Prosecutors, however, allege that the company did not possess any special technology capable of decrypting the ransomware as represented. Instead, Pinhasi allegedly contacted the cybercriminals who had attacked his clients and paid them for decryption keys. MonsterCloud employees then used those keys in attempts to restore the affected files, according to the DOJ. Pinhasi allegedly concealed the ransom payments from clients while charging them fees that were substantially higher than the amounts paid to the attackers.$8,200 ransom, $150,000 client billOne example cited by prosecutors illustrates the alleged markup. In August 2023, Pinhasi allegedly paid approximately $8,200 to a cybercriminal for a decryption key. The client whose files had been encrypted was reportedly charged approximately $150,000 by MonsterCloud. The difference between the ransom payment and the amount billed to the client was part of what prosecutors say made the alleged scheme profitable. Overall, Pinhasi allegedly charged MonsterCloud clients more than $19 million during the scheme. More than $8 million of that money was allegedly used to make ransom payments to cybercriminals.The allegations also raise questions about the representations made to customers about MonsterCloud's technology. The DOJ said that in May 2019, a paid spokesperson for the company asked Pinhasi whether MonsterCloud actually had proprietary software capable of decrypting ransomware. Pinhasi allegedly responded that the company did not have proprietary technology to decrypt ransomware data.Charges and possible penaltyPinhasi faces two counts of wire fraud and one count of wire fraud conspiracy. If convicted, each count carries a maximum penalty of up to 20 years in prison, according to the DOJ. The FBI is investigating the case, while prosecutors from the Justice Department's Computer Crime and Intellectual Property Section and the Eastern District of New York's National Security and Cybercrime Section are handling the prosecution. The case also comes against the backdrop of federal warnings about ransomware payments. The FBI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency have said they do not recommend paying ransomware demands because payment does not guarantee that files will be decrypted, systems will be restored or stolen information will not be leaked.For businesses facing a ransomware attack, the allegations in this case highlight another risk beyond the original cyberattack: relying on a service provider that may misrepresent how it is recovering encrypted data. Prosecutors allege that instead of providing the promised alternative to ransom payments, Pinhasi's company secretly paid the attackers and passed the cost on to already distressed victims at a substantial markup. Pinhasi has not been convicted. The charges are allegations, and he is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: 12,400 new Durga Pujas in Bengal this year: CM
articles.summary: West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari says 12,400 new Durga Pujas are approved this year, raising the total to 57,400; Rs 1 lakh grants begin Sunday.
articles.body: Kolkata: Bengal would see 12,400 new Durga Pujas this year, taking the total number from 45,000 in 2025 to 57,400 this time, chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced at the inauguration of the Durga Puja festival at Eden Gardens on Saturday evening. He said the state approved the new applicants and made arrangements to provide them with grant.“In 2025, 45,000 Durga Pujas were granted permission. This year, the nationalist, double-engine govt, which seeks to honour our culture, heritage and Sanatan traditions, has granted approval to 12,400 new applicants to hold puja. Arrangements have been made to provide them with the grants,” Adhikari said.Taking a swipe at the previous dispensation, the CM said people were earlier forced to approach the high court to organise Durga Puja. “That was a matter of grief and sorrow. This time, to my knowledge, no one had to approach the high court,” he said.The chief minister sought to position the govt’s approach as one that combined the cultural heritage of Durga Puja with its religious significance and scriptural traditions. He said the state cabinet decided that celebrations should not begin in Pitri Paksha and that the festival inauguration would instead take place during Devi Paksha.Adhikari announced that puja committees willing to accept the govt financial assistance of Rs 1 lakh would start receiving the money from Sunday. He added the govt left it to organisers of big-budget pujas to decide whether to accept the money or not, adding there would be no adverse feelings towards those declining it. “Over 200 puja committees, especially in Kolkata, said they would not take the grant,” he said. Seeking to add an international character to the festival, Adhikari said the state would work to promote Durga Puja’s heritage, tradition and scripturally guided practices globally. He credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s initiative for Durga Puja receiving Unesco’s Intangible Cultural Heritage recognition. He also acknowledged Union home minister Amit Shah’s participation in the inauguration programme at Victoria Memorial in 2023.Adhikari urged puja committees to complete idol immersion by Oct 24, saying arrangements had been made at the ghats. “The state information and cultural affairs department will recognise puja committees across categories, including best idol, best puja, environmental awareness sanctity and purity,” he added.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kolkata | Silver Rate in Kolkata | Bank Holidays in Kolkata | Public Holidays in Kolkata | Kolkata AQI | Weather in Kolkata | Petrol Price in Kolkata | Diesel Price in Kolkata | CNG Price in Kolkata | LPG Price in KolkataStay updated with the latest Kolkata news. articles.title: 8 held for kidnapping minor, forcing her into prostitution
articles.summary: Hyderabad: 8 arrested for kidnapping a 15-year-old and forcing her into prostitution in Attapur; case booked under BNS, POCSO and ITPA.
articles.body: Hyderabad: Tolichowki police have arrested eight people for kidnapping a minor girl and forcing her into prostitution in Attapur.The accused have been identified as Shaik Atif, an auto-rickshaw driver; brothel operators Sabiya Begum and Mohammed Hajimiya; and their associates Afreen alias Sana, Samreen Begum, Md Nadeem, Md Kaifuddin and Ali Bin Akram.According to police, Atif, who knew the 15-year-old girl, lured her with promises of marriage and a comfortable home. He took her in his auto-rickshaw from Tolichowki on Sept 2 and handed her over to Afreen and Samreen in Attapur. The girl is a school dropout.“The duo lured the girl with promises of food and shelter before selling her to Sabiya Begum, who runs a brothel in Attapur, for Rs 30,000. The amount was shared among Atif, Afreen and Samreen,” Tolichowki ACP Syed Fiaz said.Police said Sabiya Begum allegedly forced the girl into prostitution with the assistance of Nadeem, Kaifuddin and Ali Bin Akram, who arranged customers.The girl reportedly escaped from the brothel on Oct 5 and returned to her family. On Friday, her family approached the police and lodged a complaint.A case was registered under relevant provisions of the BNS, the Pocso Act and the Immoral Traffic (Prevention) Act.On Saturday, police arrested all eight accused in Attapur. Six mobile phones and an auto-rickshaw were seized from them.
